findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: @astudioplus/codegraph-mcp
findings.detail: 'astudioplus__codegraph-mcp' launches @astudioplus/codegraph-mcp through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["@astudioplus/codegraph-mcp@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): codegraph_get_detailed_symbol
findings.detail: The description of 'astudioplus__codegraph-mcp.codegraph_get_detailed_symbol' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: encoded_blob. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: encoded_blob, entropy, log_len, imperative_density.

evidence.description: Gets comprehensive symbol details including source code and relationships. USE WHEN: you need full context about a symbol — source code, callers, callees, complexity, and metadata together. MORE COMPLETE than get_symbol_info but heavier. Returns: symbol (name, kind, signature, visibility, uri, line_range, properties), source (full source code string), callers (array), callees (array). Toggle includeSource/includeCallers/includeCallees to control response size. Identify symbol via uri+line or nod

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

evidence.description: Searches codebase for symbols by name or pattern. USE WHEN: finding function/class implementations, exploring unfamiliar code, or locating specific functionality. THIS IS YOUR STARTING POINT when you don't know where code is located. Supports both exact name matching and natural language queries (e.g., 'function that validates email addresses'). Returns array of matches, each with: name, kind (function/class/method/variable/interface/type/module), file path, line range, signature, and docstring.

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'astudioplus__codegraph-mcp': executes commands + writes or deletes files
findings.detail: 6 combination(s) exist where one tool executes commands and another writes or deletes files. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they executes commands and writes files, so the agent can persist a payload for a later session to pick up. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
